title: MERGE Statement
description: Learn how to use the MERGE statement to synchronize data between a source and target table.

data.text: The MERGE statement allows you to perform INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations in a single statement based on whether rows in the source table match rows in the target table.
When synchronizing a source table with a target table, there are three possible cases:

items: NOT MATCHED BY TARGET: Rows exist in the source but not in the target. You need to INSERT them into the target.
MATCHED: Rows exist in both tables but have different values. You need to UPDATE the target with values from the source.
NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE: Rows exist in the target but not in the source. You need to DELETE them from the target.

data.alt: SQL Server MERGE statement illustration showing source and target tables with insert, update, and delete actions

data.title: MERGE Statement Syntax
data.content: Synchronizes a target table with data from a source table using INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE.
data.code:
MERGE target_table USING source_table
ON merge_condition
WHEN MATCHED
    THEN update_statement
WHEN NOT MATCHED
    THEN insert_statement
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE
    THEN DELETE;

items: Specify the target table and source table in the MERGE clause.
The merge_condition determines how rows from the source match rows from the target, similar to a JOIN condition. Typically, use primary key or unique key columns.
MATCHED: rows that satisfy the merge condition. Update the target with source values.
NOT MATCHED (also called NOT MATCHED BY TARGET): rows in the source with no match in the target. Insert them.
NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE: rows in the target with no match in the source. Delete them to synchronize.

data.text: The following example uses the sales.category (target) and sales.category_staging (source) tables to synchronize product category data.

data.title: Create Source and Target Tables
data.content: Creates and populates both the target and staging tables.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE sales.category (
    category_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    category_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    amount DECIMAL(10 , 2 )
);

INSERT INTO sales.category(category_id, category_name, amount)
VALUES(1,'Children Bicycles',15000),
    (2,'Comfort Bicycles',25000),
    (3,'Cruisers Bicycles',13000),
    (4,'Cyclocross Bicycles',10000);

CREATE TABLE sales.category_staging (
    category_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    category_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    amount DECIMAL(10 , 2 )
);

INSERT INTO sales.category_staging(category_id, category_name, amount)
VALUES(1,'Children Bicycles',15000),
    (3,'Cruisers Bicycles',13000),
    (4,'Cyclocross Bicycles',20000),
    (5,'Electric Bikes',10000),
    (6,'Mountain Bikes',10000);

data.title: MERGE Statement
data.content: Synchronizes the target category table with the staging table.
data.code:
MERGE sales.category t 
    USING sales.category_staging s
ON (s.category_id = t.category_id)
WHEN MATCHED
    THEN UPDATE SET 
        t.category_name = s.category_name,
        t.amount = s.amount
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET 
    THEN INSERT (category_id, category_name, amount)
         VALUES (s.category_id, s.category_name, s.amount)
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE 
    THEN DELETE;

data.alt: SQL Server MERGE example output showing synchronized category data

items: Rows with category_id 1, 3, and 4 match between source and target, so the MERGE statement updates the category name and amount in the target.
Rows with category_id 5 and 6 exist only in the source, so they are INSERTED into the target.
Row with category_id 2 exists only in the target, so it is DELETED from the target.

data.title: MERGE Key Points
points: MERGE performs INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE in a single statement.
Use the merge_condition to match rows between source and target tables.
WHEN MATCHED handles updates for existing rows.
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET handles inserts for new rows.
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE handles deletes for removed rows.
MERGE is ideal for synchronizing data between staging and production tables.
